── Step 2 of 28 · Role types ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  Site-wide objects (role types, groups, statuses, resolutions, priorities, issue link types, issue
  types and custom fields) are shared by every space on the site, so existing ones are compared,
  never changed. Missing ones with mode ensure are created; missing ones with mode reuse must be
  created first.

── Step 10 of 28 · Field contexts ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  A field's contexts give its options and default value, per space and issue type. A context used
  only by this space is created when missing, and its options, default and issue types are changed
  to match; taking an option, an issue type or a context away needs --allow-delete=contexts, and is
  blocked while work items have a value it would affect. A shared one must exist, and is never
  changed.

  ✓ exists   Change reason  matches (1 context)
  ✓ exists   Change risk    matches (1 context)
  ✓ exists   Change type    matches (1 context)
  ✓ exists   Flagged        matches (1 context)
  ✓ exists   Impact         matches (1 context)

── Step 11 of 28 · Screens ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  Screens and workflows can be used by several spaces. A managed one (mode managed, the default) is
  created for this space when missing, and changed to match the spec only while this space alone
  uses it; a change that removes something needs --allow-delete. A reused one must exist, and is
  never changed.

  ✓ exists   TS: Kanban Bug Screen   matches (id 10013)
  ✓ exists   TS: Kanban Default Issue Screen
                                     matches (id 10012)
  ✓ exists   TS: Kanban Epic Screen  matches (id 10014)

── Step 13 of 28 · Issue type scheme ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  These steps tie the space's issue types to the objects above, through schemes. A scheme the space
  uses that matches is kept; one this tool made that only this space uses is changed to match.
  Jira's own and shared schemes are never changed: when the space's scheme does not match, the one
  the spec's binding names, or a new one named after space.managed_prefix, is used instead, and step
  25 switches the space to it.

  ✓ exists   Issue type scheme  the space's, "TS: Kanban Issue Type Scheme" (id 10146), matches

── Step 17 of 28 · Permissions ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  Who may do what in the space, who is told of changes, who may see which work items, and which
  priorities it offers are schemes too, decided the same way: the space's scheme is kept when it
  matches; otherwise the one the spec's binding names, or a new one named after
  space.managed_prefix, is used, and step 25 switches the space to it. A switch that would leave
  work items without their priority or security level is blocked.

  ✓ exists   Permission scheme  the space's, "Default software scheme" (id 10002), matches

── Step 25 of 28 · Scheme switches ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
